title: Investigation of coherence and source and frequency analysis of electroencephalogram during general anaesthesia measured by intraoperative standard neuromonitoring Eclipse E4
summary: Measurement of depth of anaesthesia on a numerical scale (e.g. 0 = very deep anaesthesia, 100 = awake) is frequently used  in addition to clinical estimation of anaesthesia during surgery. A potential method for measuring depth of anaesthesia is the measurement of changes of electroencephalogram (EEG)-coherence between different brain regions. In this case coherence means an interaction of EEG-activities that are probably equivalent to communication between brain regions. NIM-ECLIPSE(TM) E4 is a measuring device enabling bedside coherence measurement during intraoperative neuromonitoring. Possibly the measurement accuracy of bedside monitoring is less reliable than standard offline analysis due to Signal disturbance and shorter EEG sequences available for analysis. Hence, in this study will be examined, if EEG-coherence measured by NIM-ECLIPSE(TM) E4 changes significantly during induction of and recovery from anaesthesia. The anonymised EEG-data can also later be analysed offline.

interventions.name:
Measurement of EEG-Coherence during induction of anaesthesia
Measurement of EEG-Coherence during recovery from anaesthesia

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Patients scheduled for surgery under general anaesthesia
Exclusion criteria:
Refusion of participation, patients inable to give informed consent, central nervous diseases, language barrier.
